prompt: Start as a survivors' camp and grow into a walled city.

card.name: Survivors' Camp to Walled City

site.text: Starts as a small survivors' camp on level ground and grows outward into a walled city within the claim

style.text: Makeshift and improvised at the core (timber, scrap, patched walls) hardening into solid stone-and-timber city architecture toward the outside

purpose.text: A survivors' refuge that grows from a camp into a defended, self-sufficient walled city

card.interpretation: You want a settlement that reads as a growth story: a ragged survivors' camp at the centre, with a proper wall and city built around it. I took the site as a ring wall on level ground within the 64-block claim, a rustic style that goes from improvised to solid, and a home-base purpose. No backstory was given, so none was added.

contradictions.issue: Camp and walled city are two stages, but only one build is made
contradictions.resolution: Both are shown at once: the camp stays as the core, with newer city buildings and the wall around it.

assumptions: Size M, fitting a 64-block claim radius
Rustic style chosen to carry the improvised-to-solid look
Terrain is flat since no landform was requested

program.notes: Oldest, patched-together gathering hall at the camp's heart; communal hearth, bunks, notice board.
Crude lean-to style cabins ringed around the old campfire; some patched with scrap.
Newer sturdier homes built as the city grew, stone footings and timber upper floors.
Original camp fire pit, now an open square with stalls.
Main gate in the city wall, with portcullis and guard room.
Forge for tools and wall repairs.
Food stores and crop plots just inside the wall.
